subject: Post-demo pulse: recommended model slate + risk lanes
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novus.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo pulse: recommended model slate + risk lanes

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps from our side so the team at Novus has actionable options for the POC. I kept this intentionally concise so you can forward into your technical thread.

TL;DR (recommended slate) — three model paths we validated against your demo prompts and the short evaluation set you shared:

1) Redwood-2.7B-quant (cost-first) — lowest per-token cost, excellent throughput with our 8-bit optimized kernel. Good for high-volume summarization and retrieval-augmented responses where hallucination tolerance is moderate.
2) Bloom-7B-rt (balanced latency/quality) — best median latency at 256/512 tokens with solid factuality on your domain prompts; recommended default for canary.
3) Llama-13B-int8 (quality-first fallback) — strongest long-form coherence and knowledge retention, higher 95th-percentile latency and cost. Use as fallback for complex synthesis jobs or customer-facing long responses.

Benchmarks & evidence: attached CSV has end-to-end median and P95 token latencies (256/512 runs), per-token cost estimates using your expected qps, and our quality sketch (ROUGE/F1 on the eval set + observed hallucination flags). Drive links and a lightweight prompt pack are included.

Key risk lanes we want to surface now:
- Latency spikes for 13B at P95 under your expected burst pattern — we recommend a dedicated warm pool for fallback nodes or an autoscale burst policy in Dedicated.
- Regression risk around list-structured outputs (bulleted meeting recaps) — Bloom-7B-rt occasionally collapses list delimiters under adversarial prompts; we have prompt-rewrites in the pack.
- Cost cliff if workload moves from short to long average token lengths — quantized 2.7B is cost-stable, 13B becomes expensive quickly.

Action items / next steps (proposed):
- Marissa: run a 512-token P95 tail-latency run on the Novus prompt set (attached) for all three candidates and paste results to the HubSpot deal record (DEAL-2028-NOVUS-17). Use the canary-rollout-template.yaml we attached for the rollout simulation.
- Monica: prepare a short hallucination regression check (50 case sample from Novus corpus) and flag failure modes.
- Alex / Priya: confirm which user journeys should default to the balanced model vs fallback to quality-first — this will drive traffic routing and cost forecasts.

Links and attachments: bench CSV, prompt pack (prompt examples and two QA templates), canary rollout template.

Would love a brief confirmation from you today/tomorrow on the routing default and any additional hard constraints (SLA, max cost/QPS) so we can finalize a canary configuration.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: novus_postdemo_benchmarks_20280901.csv (CSV), novus_prompt_pack_v1.json (JSON), canary-rollout-template.yaml (YAML)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novus.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novus.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 16:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo pulse: recommended model slate + risk lanes

Thanks Rishi — really useful summary. Two quick clarifications from our side:

1) For the user journey split, we want the default (90% of traffic) to favor latency/price for live search suggestions, and the 10% heavy-synthesis flows (report generation) to hit the quality-first path. That suggests Bloom-7B-rt as default and Llama-13B-int8 for synthesis.
2) Our procurement team requires a preliminary monthly cost estimate for expected usage: estimate based on 5M tokens/mo (mixed short/long, average 150 tokens). Can you include both hosted and Dedicated (reserved) ballparks?

Also — latency requirement is soft 300ms median for suggestion flows; hard P95 must be under 700ms. If Bloom-7B-rt with our traffic profile can meet that, we can proceed to the canary.

Alex
Head of Product — Novus AI
alex.turner@novus.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 23:40:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo pulse: recommended model slate + risk lanes

Marissa / Monica — forwarding Alex's note. Please treat this as the prioritized sprint for today:

1) Marissa: run the 512-token P95 tail-latency and median runs across the three candidates on Redwood infra using the attached prompt pack. Measure both single-request latency and small-batch (batch size 4) behavior. Paste raw numbers to HubSpot (deal: DEAL-2028-NOVUS-17) and attach the test harness log. Expected fields in CSV: model, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, throughput_rps, per_token_cost_usd.

2) Monica: execute the hallucination regression check (50 cases). Note any systematic failure modes (e.g., wrong entity merging, date hallucination, list collapse). For Bloom-7B-rt, check bullets/list output fidelity specifically. For Llama-13B-int8, focus on long-context coherence >512 tokens.

3) Both: prepare a simple cost comparison in two columns: Hosted (redwood-hosted API) vs Dedicated (monthly reserved commit), using Novus's 5M tokens/mo estimate Alex mentioned. Use our standard reserved discounts and include a sensitivity row for avg token lengths 150 vs 300.

I'll draft a short canary config: route 5% traffic to Llama-13B-int8 as fallback with auto-evict on P95 > 800ms, 90% to Bloom-7B-rt, 5% to Redwood-2.7B-quant for bulk cheap ops. Attach the canary-rollout-template.yaml once it's ready.

If either of you see a red flag in the 13B P95 runs we should propose a warm-pool or pre-warmed standby for the fallback. Deliverables by EOD PST tomorrow so procurement has numbers.

Thanks — Rishi
